## Load all packages
```{r}

library("rlang")
library("Seurat");
library("sctransform");
library("dplyr");
library("RColorBrewer");
library("ggthemes");
library("ggplot2");
library("cowplot");
library("data.table");
library("scales")

```


## Set up Seurat object
```{r}

memory.limit(size=50000000)

samples=c("xu44","xu46")

data.10x = list()

data.10x[[1]] <- Read10X(data.dir = "xu44_SPM/raw_feature_bc_matrix");

data.10x[[2]] <- Read10X(data.dir = "xu46_SPM/raw_feature_bc_matrix");


## Convert each feature-barcode matrix to a Seurat object.

SPM.list = list(); 

SPM.list[[1]] = CreateSeuratObject(counts = data.10x[[1]], min.cells=3, min.features=200, project=samples[1]);

SPM.list[[1]][["DataSet"]] = samples[1];

SPM.list[[2]] = CreateSeuratObject(counts = data.10x[[2]], min.cells=3, min.features=200, project=samples[2]);

SPM.list[[2]][["DataSet"]] = samples[2];


### Subset each library to filter low quality cells


SPM.list[[1]] <- subset(SPM.list[[1]], subset = nCount_RNA > 5000 & nFeature_RNA > 1000 & nCount_RNA < 150000 & nFeature_RNA < 15000)

SPM.list[[2]] <- subset(SPM.list[[2]], subset = nCount_RNA > 5000 & nFeature_RNA > 1000 & nCount_RNA < 150000 & nFeature_RNA < 15000)


## logNormalize

SPM.list[[1]]<- NormalizeData(SPM.list[[1]], normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000)

SPM.list[[2]]<- NormalizeData(SPM.list[[2]], normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000)


## Find variables


SPM.list[[1]]<- FindVariableFeatures(SPM.list[[1]], selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)

SPM.list[[2]]<- FindVariableFeatures(SPM.list[[2]], selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)



## Select features that are repeatedly variable across datasets for integration


features <- SelectIntegrationFeatures(object.list = SPM.list)


## find anchors

anchors <- FindIntegrationAnchors(object.list = SPM.list, anchor.features = features)


## Integrate data

SPM.int <- IntegrateData(anchorset = anchors)


DefaultAssay(SPM.int)<-"integrated"


# Run the standard workflow for visualization and clustering
SPM.int <- ScaleData(SPM.int, verbose = FALSE)
SPM.int <- RunPCA(SPM.int, npcs = 30, verbose = FALSE)

## Determine the ‘dimensionality’ of the dataset

ElbowPlot(SPM.int, ndims = 40)

## Elbow plot: quantitative approach
## https://hbctraining.github.io/scRNA-seq/lessons/elbow_plot_metric.html

## Calculate the first metric:
## Determine percent of variation associated with each PC
pct <- SPM.int[["pca"]]@stdev / sum(SPM.int[["pca"]]@stdev) * 100

# Calculate cumulative percents for each PC
cumu <- cumsum(pct)

# Determine which PC exhibits cumulative percent greater than 90% and % variation associated with the PC as less than 5
co1 <- which(cumu > 90 & pct < 5)[1]

co1


# Determine the difference between variation of PC and subsequent PC
co2 <- sort(which((pct[1:length(pct) - 1] - pct[2:length(pct)]) > 0.1), decreasing = T)[1] + 1

# last point where change of % of variation is more than 0.1%.
co2

# Minimum of the two calculation
pcs <- min(co1, co2)

pcs

```



```{r}
SPM.int <- RunUMAP(SPM.int, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:pcs) ## Use PC number based on above Elbow plot: quantitative approach

SPM.int <- FindNeighbors(SPM.int, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:pcs)

SPM.int <- FindClusters(SPM.int, resolution = 0.8)

# Visualization

DimPlot(SPM.int, reduction = "umap", label = TRUE, pt.size = 1)
DimPlot(SPM.int, reduction = "umap", group.by = "orig.ident")

## two plots next to each other 

p1 <- DimPlot(SPM.int, reduction = "umap", group.by = "orig.ident", pt.size = 1)
p2 <- DimPlot(SPM.int, reduction = "umap", label = TRUE, repel = TRUE, pt.size = 1, label.size = 10)
p1 + p2

### split the UMAPs by samples 

DimPlot(SPM.int, reduction = "umap", split.by = "orig.ident", pt.size = 1)


### group the UMAPs by samples. 

DimPlot(SPM.int, reduction = "umap", group.by = "orig.ident", pt.size = 1)


## Remove cluster with low UMI or doublet

SPM.int_rmDB <- subset(SPM.int, idents = 1, invert = TRUE)

DimPlot(SPM.int_rmDB, reduction = "umap", label = TRUE, pt.size = 1)


### split the integrated object to re-normalize and process

SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list <- SplitObject(SPM.int_rmDB, split.by = "orig.ident")

SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list


## set RNA assay before normalization and processing 

DefaultAssay(SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[1]]) <- "RNA"
DefaultAssay(SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[2]]) <- "RNA"


## logNormalize

SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[1]]<- NormalizeData(SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[1]], normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000)

SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[2]]<- NormalizeData(SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[2]], normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000)


## Find variables


SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[1]]<- FindVariableFeatures(SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[1]], selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)

SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[2]]<- FindVariableFeatures(SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list[[2]], selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)



# select features that are repeatedly variable across datasets for integration


features <- SelectIntegrationFeatures(object.list = SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list)


# find anchors

anchors <- FindIntegrationAnchors(object.list = SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.list, anchor.features = features)


# Integrate data
# this command creates an 'integrated' data assay

SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.int <- IntegrateData(anchorset = anchors)


DefaultAssay(SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.int)<-"integrated"


# Run the standard workflow for visualization and clustering
SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.int <- ScaleData(SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.int, verbose = FALSE)
SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.int <- RunPCA(SPM_int.rmDB.recluster.int, npcs = 30, verbose = FALSE)


```

ElbowPlot(subcluster.vasculature.Sphase, ndims = 40)

## Elbow plot: quantitative approach
## https://hbctraining.github.io/scRNA-seq/lessons/elbow_plot_metric.html

# Determine percent of variation associated with each PC

# Calculate cumulative percents for each PC

# Determine which PC exhibits cumulative percent greater than 90% and % variation associated with the PC as less than 5

co1

co2 <- sort(which((pct[1:length(pct) - 1] - pct[2:length(pct)]) > 0.1), decreasing = T)[1] + 1

# last point where change of % of variation is more than 0.1%.
co2

```{r}

library(Seurat)

## 1) load the already-annotated object
SPM.final <- readRDS("SPM.final.rds")

## 2) final cluster colors
cluster.colors <- c(
  "Cortex"="#afbca5","Pith"="#99b6ca","S.Phase.(non.epi)"="#95511f",
  "G2.M.Phase.(non.epi.II)"="#e761d8","Determinate.Lateral.Organ.(epi)"="#98fb98",
  "Meristem.Epidermis"="#66dcf6","Meristem.Tip.(stem.cell)"="#e93f33",
  "Determinate.Lateral.Organ.(non.epi)"="#64ac4e","Meristem.Base"="#f3f550",
  "G2.M.Phase.(non.epi.I)"="#737172","S.Phase.(epi)"="#e9967a",
  "G2.M.Phase.(epi)"="#808000","Adaxial.Meristem.Periphery.(non.epi)"="#4d6dcb",
  "Vasculature"="#ffa500","TBD(exp.FCP1.but.not.CLE7)"="#F68282",
  "TBD.I"="#F8766D","TBD.II"="#D4D915","Stem.epidermis"="#B95FBB")

## 3) check that the saved identities match the color names
cur <- as.character(Idents(SPM.final))
print(table(cur))
missing <- setdiff(unique(cur), names(cluster.colors))
if (length(missing) > 0) stop("These labels have no color: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))

## 4) set identity levels in color order
Idents(SPM.final) <- factor(cur, levels = names(cluster.colors)[names(cluster.colors) %in% cur])

## 5) store labels, per-cell colors, and the palette in the object
SPM.final$final_annotation <- as.character(Idents(SPM.final))
SPM.final$final_color <- unname(cluster.colors[SPM.final$final_annotation])
SPM.final@misc$cluster_colors <- cluster.colors

## 6) check the plot, then save under a new name
DimPlot(SPM.final, reduction = "umap", label = TRUE, label.size = 5, pt.size = 1,
        cols = SPM.final@misc$cluster_colors)

saveRDS(SPM.final, file = "SPM.final.updated.color.rds")


```
